Voxel-wise Modeling Module¶

Voxel-wise encoding models represent a cornerstone of modern fMRI analysis, allowing researchers to quantify how well various stimulus features (e.g., from AI models) predict brain activity at the level of individual voxels or vertices across the cortex. This approach moves beyond traditional univariate analyses to build predictive models of brain responses, offering fine-grained insights into neural representations.

The voxelwise_modeling module within neursen_reveal provides the tools to construct and evaluate these encoding models. It aligns AI-derived features with BOLD fMRI signals, trains linear regression models for each brain location, and computes metrics like R-squared scores, which indicate the proportion of variance in brain activity explained by the AI model’s features. This direct mapping helps answer questions about what information specific brain regions encode, and how closely artificial systems’ representations align with biological ones. By providing flexible parameters like delayers and cross-validation strategies, this module enables rigorous and robust brain modeling.

Function Reference¶

This module includes functions for generating model scores, rendering these scores on brain surfaces, averaging model scores across subjects then rendering the averaged score on brain surface.

neursen_reveal.voxelwise_modeling.generate_scores_for_specific_model_across_subjects(Bold_dataset_dir: str, features_file_path: str, saving_dir: str, bold_test: list, save_EV: bool = False, verbose: bool = True, random_seed: int = None, delayers: list = [1, 2, 3, 4], n_runs_out: int = 1)[source]¶

Orchestrates the entire voxel-wise modeling process for multiple subjects, adhering to a BIDS-like directory structure (sub-XX/ses-XX/func/.nii).

This function iterates through subjects, prepares their BOLD and feature data, trains a VoxelWiseModeler, computes and saves R-squared scores, and optionally computes and saves explainable variance (EV).

Parameters¶

Bold_dataset_dirstr

Path to the root directory containing subject BOLD data following BIDS. Expected structure: Bold_dataset_dir/sub-XX/ses-XX/func/*.nii.

features_file_pathstr

Full path to the HDF5 (.h5) file containing extracted stimuli features.

saving_dirstr

Root directory where results (scores, best_alphas, EV) will be saved. Results will be organized by subject.

bold_testlist, optional

A list of string identifiers that identify the BOLD signals to be used for testing.

save_EVbool, optional

If True, compute and save explainable variance (EV) for test runs. Defaults to False.

verbosebool, optional

If True, print detailed progress messages during execution. Defaults to True.

random_seedint, optional

Seed for reproducibility of model fitting and cross-validation. Defaults to None (no fixed seed).

delayerslist, optional

List of time-step delays to use for the VoxelWiseModeler. Defaults to [1, 2, 3, 4].

n_runs_outint, optional

Number of runs to leave out for validation in each cross-validation fold during model fitting. Defaults to 1 (Leave-One-Run-Out).

neursen_reveal.voxelwise_modeling.render_scores(scores: ndarray, threshold: str = '90%', title: str = 'Rendered R-squared Scores')[source]¶

Renders voxel-wise scores (e.g., R-squared) onto an inflated brain surface using nilearn.plotting.view_surf.

This function assumes hcp_utils is configured correctly to provide mesh data (hcp.mesh.inflated, hcp.mesh.sulc) and cortex data.

Parameters¶

scoresnp.ndarray

A NumPy array of scores for each voxel/vertex. Shape: (n_voxels,).

thresholdstr or float, optional

Threshold for displaying values on the surface map. Can be a percentage string (e.g., “90%”) or a float (e.g., 0.1). Defaults to “90%”.

titlestr, optional

Title for the rendered brain plot. Defaults to “Rendered R-squared Scores”.

Returns¶

nilearn.plotting.html_view.HTMLView

An interactive HTML viewer object of the brain surface plot.

neursen_reveal.voxelwise_modeling.render_averaged_scores(data_dir: str, threshold: str = '90%', title: str = 'Averaged Rendered R-squared Scores')[source]¶

Calculates the average R-squared scores across all subjects for a given model and renders them onto an inflated brain surface.

This function expects data_dir to contain subdirectories, each with a scores.npy file for a different subject.

Parameters¶

data_dirstr

The path to the directory containing subject-specific score subdirectories. Expected structure: data_dir/sub-XX/scores.npy.

thresholdstr or float, optional

Threshold for displaying values on the surface map. Can be a percentage string (e.g., “90%”) or a float (e.g., 0.1). Defaults to “90%”.

titlestr, optional

Title for the rendered brain plot. Defaults to “Averaged Rendered R-squared Scores”.

Returns¶

nilearn.plotting.html_view.HTMLView

An interactive HTML viewer object of the averaged brain surface plot. Returns None if rendering fails.

Example Usage¶

This example illustrates the two-step process: first, generating voxel-wise R-squared scores, and then visualizing the averaged results across subjects on a brain surface.

```

from neursen_reveal.voxelwise_modeling import generate_scores_for_specific_model_across_subjects

from neursen_reveal.voxelwise_modeling import render_averaged_scores

import os

import numpy as np # May be needed for advanced custom plotting after generation

# — Step 1: Generate Voxel-wise Scores —

# Define placeholder paths for your data and output

CLEANED_BOLD_ROOT = “/path/to/your/cleaned_bids_data”

FEATURES_FILE = “/path/to/your/extracted_features/my_ai_model_features.h5”

SCORES_OUTPUT_DIR = “/path/to/your/voxelwise_scores_output”

# Ensure the output directory for scores exists

os.makedirs(SCORES_OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

print(”— Generating voxel-wise R-squared scores across subjects —“)

generate_scores_for_specific_model_across_subjects(

Bold_dataset_dir=CLEANED_BOLD_ROOT,

features_file_path=FEATURES_FILE,

saving_dir=SCORES_OUTPUT_DIR,

bold_test=[‘task-testrun’], # Specify the functional run(s) to use as test set

delayers=[1, 2, 3, 4], # Common hemodynamic delays in TRs

n_runs_out=1, # Leave one run out for cross-validation

verbose=True,

random_seed=42 # For reproducibility

)

print(f”Voxel-wise scores generated for each subject and saved to: {SCORES_OUTPUT_DIR}”)

# — Step 2: Render Averaged Scores on Brain Surface —

print(”n— Rendering averaged R-squared scores on brain surface —“)

# render_averaged_scores expects the directory containing the subject-level scores.npy files.

render_averaged_scores(

data_dir=SCORES_OUTPUT_DIR,

threshold=”95%”, # Show only the top 5% of scores

title=”Averaged Encoding Performance (AI Model X)”

)

print(“Interactive brain plot of averaged scores generated (will open in browser/notebook).”)
